entries.7c56df04e3052ba9: This is an analysis tool for consumer goods manufacturers that grasps consumer purchasing trends nationwide and by region to support decision-making. Based on ID-POS data linked to purchaser attributes, it has the speed to detect purchases up to the day before yesterday. It is cloud-based and provided as a recurring-revenue model, in principle on annual contracts, and the number of client companies was 180 as of the end of March 2026. Sales to external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥895 million.

entries.bce1367f05eb8428: Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,870 million, up 20.3% from the previous year. By breakdown, “Eagle Eye” accounted for ¥895 million, “Shopping Scan” for ¥383 million, and other items for ¥592 million. The factors cited for the revenue increase are the rollout of retail DX services and AI solutions for major retailers, and growth in the number of companies under contract for “Eagle Eye.”
entries.be670fa401208953: It is stated that its distinguishing feature is the ability to provide value to customer companies across all three areas needed for data utilization: (1) data, (2) technology and (3) know-how for utilization. It is stated that the refinement process, which standardizes large volumes of purchase data with specifications differing by retailer, requires substantial effort and know-how, and that this makes the business model difficult to imitate.

Through providing a "decision-making platform (OS)" that combines purchase data spanning physical stores to EC with AI, it says it will build a mechanism that lets companies curb excessive resource input into the market and reduce inventory and disposal losses through supply-demand optimization.
